title: OpenTofu & Terraform Infrastructure Automation, State & Modules
summary: Master enterprise infrastructure automation with OpenTofu and Terraform: declarative HCL syntax, provider configurations, remote state locking with S3 and DynamoDB, for_each meta-arguments, resource import, and refactoring with moved blocks.
learningObjectives: Structure production OpenTofu / Terraform codebases with reusable modules, input variables, and typed outputs.
Implement remote backend state storage with cryptographic locking to prevent concurrent state corruption.
Execute zero-downtime refactoring workflows using terraform import, moved blocks, and lifecycle preconditions.

curriculumModules.title: OpenTofu Architecture, HCL Syntax & State Management
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: OpenTofu (Linux Foundation fork of Terraform) uses HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL) to model infrastructure as a resource graph. State files (terraform.tfstate) map real-world cloud IDs to declarative definitions. Remote state backends (S3 + DynamoDB or Consul) enforce state locking to prevent write collisions.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Mandate encrypted remote S3 backends with DynamoDB state locking, enable versioning on state buckets, and forbid local state files in production repositories.

curriculumModules.title: Meta-Arguments, Modules & Zero-Downtime Refactoring
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Meta-arguments (for_each, count, depends_on, lifecycle) parameterize resource generation across availability zones. The moved block allows declarative resource renaming without triggering destroy-and-recreate cycles, while tofu import brings legacy infrastructure under management.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Pin provider versions strictly, enforce automated tfsec / trivy config security scans in CI pipelines, and require plan approval before apply in production environments.

labs.title: Provisioning Cloud Infrastructure with OpenTofu / Terraform
labs.scenario: Initialize and apply an infrastructure stack in directory /infra: create main.tf declaring an AWS VPC aws_vpc.main and an EKS cluster aws_eks_cluster.prod, run tofu init to configure providers, and execute tofu apply -auto-approve to provision cloud resources.
labs.productionContext: Declarative IaC with OpenTofu ensures deterministic, reproducible environment provisioning across dev, staging, and production without manual console drift.
objectives: Create /infra/main.tf with aws_vpc and aws_eks_cluster resources.
Run tofu init to initialize provider plugins.
Run tofu apply to provision cloud resources and generate state.

labs.title: Configuring Remote S3 Backend State with DynamoDB Locking
labs.scenario: To prevent concurrent state corruption, configure a remote S3 backend in /infra/backend.tf: specify backend 's3' with bucket 'kubelabs-terraform-state', key 'prod/terraform.tfstate', region 'us-east-1', and dynamodb_table 'terraform-locks'. Execute tofu init to configure the backend.
labs.productionContext: Remote state with distributed locking prevents disastrous race conditions when multiple team members or CI runners execute simultaneous terraform apply operations.
objectives: Configure bucket, key, and dynamodb_table locking.
Run tofu init to validate backend configuration.

steps.instruction: Run tofu init to configure the S3 backend and DynamoDB state lock.

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Validation fails on missing backend configuration or unexecuted tofu init.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: /infra/backend.tf is missing required properties or tofu init was not run.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Ensure /infra/backend.tf contains backend "s3" and dynamodb_table, then execute tofu init.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why is remote state locking (e.g. via DynamoDB with an S3 backend) essential for enterprise Terraform / OpenTofu usage?
options: It speeds up network download times by caching container images in DynamoDB.
It prevents race conditions where two engineers or CI pipelines run concurrent 'apply' operations, which could corrupt or overwrite the remote state file.
It automatically commits code changes to GitHub when resources are created.
It bypasses cloud provider IAM authentication.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: State locking ensures mutual exclusion: when an operation modifies state, a lock item is written to DynamoDB. Concurrent operations fail immediately with a state lock error, preventing corrupted state files.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the 'moved' block introduced in modern Terraform and OpenTofu?
options: To migrate resources between cloud providers without changing resource types.
To record declarative resource address refactorings (e.g. from module.old to module.new) so that Terraform updates state addresses instead of destroying and recreating real-world cloud resources.
To physically move virtual machines to another AWS availability zone.
To archive unused terraform state files to Glacier.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The 'moved' block provides safe, declarative refactoring in HCL. When renaming a resource or moving it into a module, Terraform renames the address in state rather than destroying the existing infrastructure and creating a new one.
